title: MERGE-XAI-SYNC C-14 (ADOPT 01 §3 S1, grove-off worktree fallback) — the upstream deprecation: on a host where grove worktrees are unavailable (the NFS deployment class), a worktree create request SILENTLY degrades to the copy/btrfs fallback (the xai-fast-worktree crate), with no error surfaced. RECON CASE (record-only, never fails; the row reports RECON, not PASS/FAIL): the HERMETIC-MAC ARM exercises the grove-OFF path on a non-NFS host — one headless turn on sol (L-01) runs a SELF-CLEANING git probe in the hermetic temp cwd (a recon case may contain the write; disclosed in the contract): git init -q . + git config (throwaway identity, smoke@example.invalid) + git worktree add -q ../mxai-c14-wt + git worktree remove — the add+remove pair leaves no residue in the run dir and the temp cwd is discarded with the run (the probe touches only the hermetic tempdir; the real worktree is never written). EXPECTED SHAPE (recorded, not scored): the worktree add SUCCEEDS SILENTLY (the copy/btrfs fallback under our deployment class) and NO error surfaces on the wire or in the final text; the terminal carries 'WT-OUTCOME ok C14-DONE'. RECON SURFACE: (1) the final-text head (the WT-OUTCOME terminal + any error text), (2) the error-event record (absent = the silent-degrade expectation held), (3) the wire record of the git-output context (the function_call_output carrying the git result lines). The DEPLOYMENT-CLASS ARM (the real S1 claim: the NFS host where grove is genuinely off) is OPERATOR-DRIVEN on SCS per 06 §5 (the fleet-ops question, not a merge gate — 06 §5 non-goal): the README runbook documents the comparison (hermetic-arm record vs SCS-arm record; a SURFACED worktree error on either arm = the deprecation regressed under our code = new finding, report-and-stop). No scored pins by design.

args.command: git init -q . && git config user.email smoke@example.invalid && git config user.name smoke && git worktree add -q ../mxai-c14-wt && rc=$?; git worktree remove -q ../mxai-c14-wt 2>/dev/null; exit $rc

steps.prompt: Use the run_terminal_command tool to run this single command (it chains a throwaway git init, a worktree add, and a self-cleanup worktree remove, so it leaves no residue): git init -q . && git config user.email smoke@example.invalid && git config user.name smoke && git worktree add -q ../mxai-c14-wt && rc=$?; git worktree remove -q ../mxai-c14-wt 2>/dev/null; exit $rc — then reply with exactly: WT-OUTCOME <ok|error> C14-DONE, where <ok|error> reflects whether the 'git worktree add' step succeeded; if it errored, also include the error text after the token.

steps.note: ARM SCOPE (recon_note, non-scoring): the hermetic-Mac arm exercises the grove-OFF fallback path (xai-fast-worktree) on a NON-NFS host — the expected record is a SILENT success (copy/btrfs worktree, no error surfaced on the wire or in the final text; terminal 'WT-OUTCOME ok C14-DONE'). The 06 C-14 DEPLOYMENT-CLASS claim (the NFS host where grove is genuinely unavailable) is the operator arm on SCS per 06 §5 (explicit non-goal: 'No fleet-wide Grove dependency audit beyond C-14's deployment-class check — that is a fleet-ops question for the operator'); the README runbook documents the pair comparison. The self-cleaning probe (add+remove in one command, throwaway identity) keeps the recon case's contained write inside the hermetic temp cwd (disclosed in the title).

ndjson.label: ERROR-EVENT RECORD (recon, never fails): the last ndjson error event's message, if any — ABSENT = the silent-degrade expectation held (no worktree error surfaced; the 06 C-14 'no error surfaced' claim on the reachable arm). PRESENT = a surfaced worktree error = the deprecation regressed under our code = new finding -> report-and-stop (adjudicate on the record).

wire.label: VERDICT RECORD (recon, never fails): the merged ndjson final-text head — the expected shape is 'WT-OUTCOME ok C14-DONE' (the worktree add+remove probe succeeded silently). 'WT-OUTCOME error C14-DONE' (or the token absent) = the fallback surfaced a failure on this arm = new finding (adjudicate with the wire git-output record below). recon — always records, never fails.

GIT-OUTPUT RECORD (recon, all sol requests): the command + result context on the wire (the run_terminal_command call carrying the probe command, the function_call_output carrying the git result lines) — the coordinator's corpus for the hermetic-arm vs SCS-arm pair comparison (the S1 drift row's deployment-class half). recon — always records, never fails.
